newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BELGIAN POLICE DETAIN 120 AT WORLD CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELGIAN POLICE DETAIN 120 AT WORLD CUP TIE.

text.p: Belgian police said on Saturday they had detained 120 football supporters before and during a World Cup clash between Belgium and the Netherlands which the Dutch side won 3-0.

"Of the 120, 91 are from the Netherlands. The rest are Belgian," police spokesman Michael Jonniaux said. "There were no incidents in the stadium but it's the end of the match now so we have to see what happens outside."
Jonniaux said 10 of the arrests were likely to result in charges.
Belgian police deployed more than 1,500 officers, 150 mounted policemen, water cannon and 20 dog teams throughout Brussels for the match.
The match was played at the Heysel stadium where 39 fans died after Juventas and Liverpool supporters clashed at the European Cup final in 1985.
The stadium has since been rebuilt and renamed after former Belgian monarch King Baudouin, whose brother King Albert II watched the game.
